The Region

North America Is Not
a Consolation Prize

The assumption that a domestic or near-international trip is somehow less than a transatlantic one is a bias worth examining. California's wine country in October sits alongside Burgundy and Tuscany as one of the great food and wine experiences in the world. Alaska's remote wilderness lodges offer access to brown bear behavior, humpback feeding grounds, and glacier landscapes that no other continent can match. The Canadian Rockies in spring — before the summer crowds — produce some of the most extraordinary mountain scenery available to a traveler flying coach class from a domestic departure gate.

What North American travel often lacks is the planning rigor that international trips naturally attract. People book a Napa weekend without understanding that the difference between a private barrel tasting at an estate not open to the general public and a walk-in tasting room visit is not a small one. They book an Alaska cruise without understanding that a small-ship expedition to the Inside Passage and Glacier Bay is a fundamentally different experience from a large-vessel port-stop itinerary.

We plan North American travel with the same level of specificity we apply to any other region — the right properties, the right access, the right time of year. The result is usually a trip that surprises people who thought they already knew what domestic travel could be.

Where We Send Clients

Six North American Destinations Worth Planning Properly

Each rewards genuine planning — the kind that turns a good trip into one you recommend to everyone you know for the next two years.

Destination Photography · Napa & Sonoma
California Wine Country
Napa & Sonoma
Two valleys, two personalities, one of the great food and wine regions on earth. Napa for the grand estates — Cabernet Sauvignon, hillside caves, tasting rooms that require no introduction. Sonoma for the working farms, the quieter roads, and the winemakers who still answer their own phone. Harvest season in September and October is the window worth planning around — the valleys are alive in a way that no other time of year replicates. Private barrel tastings, estate dinners, and vineyard stays are available to travelers who know to ask.
Wine Country Culinary Private Estates September – October

Destination Photography · Hawaii
Pacific Islands · USA
Hawaii
No passport, no currency exchange, and one of the most naturally spectacular island chains on earth. Maui for the Road to Hana and Kaanapali coast. The Big Island for Kilauea's lava fields and manta ray night dives. Kauai for the Na Pali cliffs. Multi-island itineraries in private vacation rentals deliver a depth that a single-resort stay can't approach.
No PassportMulti-IslandYear-Round

Destination Photography · Alaska
Pacific Northwest · USA
Alaska
The last genuinely wild destination accessible from a U.S. domestic departure gate. Remote wilderness lodges in Katmai and Kenai Fjords for brown bear and humpback whale encounters. Small-ship expedition cruises through the Inside Passage and Glacier Bay — a fundamentally different experience from a large-vessel port-stop itinerary. Best late June through August.

Destination Photography · New York City
Northeast · USA
New York & the Northeast
New York City for the full experience — a hotel within walking distance of what actually matters, a food itinerary that doesn't start at Times Square, a Broadway performance that requires knowing which shows are worth the ticket price. The Northeast in fall is one of the great seasonal travel experiences: Vermont foliage, coastal Maine, the Berkshires. September and October is when this region is at its best.

Destination Photography · Canadian Rockies
Western Canada
Canadian Rockies
Banff and Jasper national parks contain some of the most dramatic mountain scenery on the continent — turquoise glacial lakes, icefields, elk and grizzly sightings within park boundaries. The Rocky Mountaineer rail journey between Vancouver and Banff is one of the finest train experiences in the world. Best May through June before the summer crowds, and late September when the larches turn gold and the elk are in rut.
BanffJasperRocky Mountaineer

Destination Photography · New Orleans
Gulf South · USA
New Orleans
The most culturally specific city in the United States — a place with its own architecture, its own cuisine, its own music tradition, and its own relationship with time. The French Quarter for the layered history. Frenchmen Street for the live music that doesn't start until midnight. A neighborhood restaurant dinner that no website recommends. Best September through November and during Jazz Fest in late April and early May.

Featured Itineraries

Trips We Plan Often

North American itineraries we've refined over many runs — and built around the access and details that don't come from searching online.

Itinerary Photography
Harvest Season · Napa Valley
September – October · 5–7 days
Napa Harvest & Sonoma Deep Dive
Four nights in Napa during crush — a private barrel tasting at a hillside estate not open to walk-ins, a winemaker lunch at a family property in Rutherford, and a restaurant dinner that requires knowing which nights the chef is actually in the kitchen. Two nights in Sonoma for a smaller-scale counterpoint: a working farm stay, a late-afternoon oyster stop in Marshall, and a winery run by a couple whose wines are on two restaurant lists and nothing else.
California5–7 Days
Itinerary Photography
Katmai & Kenai · Alaska
Late June – August · 8–10 days
Alaska Wilderness Lodge Week
Anchorage for one night, then a floatplane to a remote lodge on the Katmai coast for four days — brown bears fishing the Brooks Falls salmon run, humpback whales in Shelikof Strait, and a staff-to-guest ratio that makes a small African camp feel crowded. Kenai Fjords by small boat for the glacier calving and sea otter nurseries. A final night in Homer for the halibut fishing if the group wants it. The most concentrated wildlife experience available from a U.S. departure gate.
Alaska8–10 Days
Itinerary Photography
Banff & Jasper · Canadian Rockies
May – June & September · 8–10 days
Canadian Rockies by Rail & Road
The Rocky Mountaineer from Vancouver to Banff in its Gold Leaf dome car — two days of mountain scenery at the pace the landscape deserves, with meals that match. Three nights in Banff: Moraine Lake at dawn before the shuttle buses arrive, a Banff Springs dinner, and a guided wildlife morning in the Bow Valley. Drive north to Jasper for three nights — Maligne Lake, the Columbia Icefield Skywalk, and an evening elk walk in the townsite. One of the finest rail journeys in the world on either side of a spectacular drive.
Canada8–10 Days
Itinerary Photography
French Quarter · New Orleans
September – November · 4–5 days
New Orleans in the Right Week
A French Quarter hotel within walking distance of Frenchmen Street. A guided food tour through the Tremé with a local culinary historian — not the tourist circuit, but the neighborhood places that have been feeding the same families for three generations. A po'boy at a lunch counter, a dinner at a Creole institution that requires knowing to book six weeks out, and a late night at a Frenchmen Street club where the house band plays until 2 a.m. and the set list is different every night. Four days that take most clients years to stop talking about.
Louisiana4–5 Days

What We Add to North American Travel

Culinary historians in New Orleans, glaciologists on Alaska expedition vessels, winemakers in Napa who take private groups during crush, naturalist guides in Jasper who have worked the same valley for twenty years. When to Go

North America by Season

Fall
September – November
The best travel window for Napa and Sonoma (harvest), the Northeast (foliage), New Orleans (cooler, pre-holiday quiet), and the Canadian Rockies (larch season in late September, elk rut, lower occupancy). Multiple exceptional destinations all at their peak simultaneously — and at meaningfully lower rates than summer.
Best Overall Window
Summer
June – August
Alaska's primary window — late June through August for bear viewing at peak salmon runs, humpback feeding activity, and the longest daylight hours. Hawaii is excellent year-round but books early for summer. The Canadian Rockies and national parks are at full visitor capacity in July and August — shoulder dates (early June, late August) offer the same scenery with significantly smaller crowds.
Winter & Spring
December – May
New York City at the holidays is a genuine experience — the right hotel, the right shows, the right restaurants before the December rush. New Orleans during Jazz Fest (late April, early May) is the single best week in the city's calendar. Hawaii is exceptional in winter — whale season runs December through April on Maui. Canadian Rockies in winter offer ice skating on frozen lakes and skiing at Sunshine Village.

A Note from Mark

On North American Travel

Mark Sole
Founder & Travel Director · Hit Your Mark Travel

"The clients who are most surprised by what a North American trip can be are usually the ones who assumed they already knew. They've been to Napa before — they did a tasting room weekend in their twenties — and they don't realize that a private barrel tasting at an estate during harvest, with a winemaker who's been there twenty years and still finds it interesting to explain what the vintage is doing, is a categorically different experience. The same logic applies to Alaska, to the Canadian Rockies, to New Orleans. Every one of these destinations has a version that most people visit and a version that most people don't know how to find. That's the version worth planning."

Common Questions

North America — FAQ

Questions about national parks, wine country, the Pacific Coast, and when a travel advisor actually adds value for North America travel.

What are the best national parks to base a North America trip around?+
Yellowstone and Grand Teton in Wyoming is one of the great natural combinations — wolves, bears, bison, geysers, and alpine scenery accessible even to non-hikers. Zion and Bryce Canyon in Utah offer dramatic canyon landscapes. The Canadian Rockies (Banff and Jasper) are extraordinary for mountain scenery. Glacier National Park in Montana is one of the least-crowded spectacular parks in the system.
Which wine regions are worth building a North America trip around?+
Napa Valley and Sonoma in California offer the deepest concentration of world-class wineries, Michelin-star dining, and luxury accommodation in North America. Willamette Valley in Oregon is Pinot Noir country with a fraction of the crowds and extraordinary access to cult producers. Both have detailed winery route guides in the travel journal with specific itineraries and stops.
What is the best way to experience the Pacific Coast?+
The Pacific Coast Highway from San Francisco south through Big Sur, Carmel-by-the-Sea, and Santa Barbara to Los Angeles is one of the world's great road journeys. North from San Francisco to Mendocino, the coast is wilder and less traveled. Adding Napa or Sonoma wine country to a Northern California road trip adds depth without significant detour.
What are the best city destinations in North America?+
New York and San Francisco are the most globally recognized, each with extraordinary food, cultural, and accommodation options. Chicago, New Orleans, Portland, Austin, and Nashville have distinct characters and often reward travelers who have already done the gateway cities. Montreal and Vancouver are exceptional Canadian alternatives with very different personalities.
When is travel advisor value highest for North America?+
For national parks (permit access, guide bookings, lodge reservations that sell out far in advance), private ranch stays, remote backcountry lodges, and culinary access — the same access advantages apply as with international travel. Where I add most value is connecting experiences into a coherent itinerary rather than a series of independent bookings that don't build on each other.
What's the best time of year for different North American regions?+
Southwest (Utah, Arizona): fall and spring avoid extreme heat. Yellowstone: June–September for full wildlife access, with the elk rut in late September being spectacular. Pacific Coast: May–September for stable weather. Wine country (Napa, Willamette): September–October for harvest. Canadian Rockies: July–early September for snow-free mountain access. Alaska: June–August for maximum light and wildlife activity.
What makes Alaska worth the effort?+
Alaska in summer delivers glaciers, bear viewing on salmon streams, whale watching, and remote wilderness on a scale unlike anywhere else in North America. Denali National Park, the Kenai Peninsula, and Kodiak Island each offer extraordinary wildlife access. Small-ship cruising through the Inside Passage is one of the most scenic journeys in the world. The effort is real — but so is the reward.
Can I combine a national park trip with luxury accommodation?+
Yes. The private dude ranch and wilderness lodge category in North America is exceptional — properties in Wyoming, Montana, and Colorado combine genuine wildness with outstanding food and accommodation. Rates at properties like Triple Creek Ranch or The Ranch at Rock Creek often include all activities, meals, and guiding. These properties sell out early and benefit from advisor relationships for access and upgrades.
